clue.text: Visitor's around building really briefly

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the last letter of the word before it goes
building means putting together afresh, so the shortened word is reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for around
the word with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A guest is said to be hanging about a building, but only for a very short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visitor's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is just 'is' joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who calls on you at home, or pays you a short social visit, is a caller.

clue.text: One uncomfortable with top-class swimmer having no pool?

blocks.note: A is the top grade, as in A-list or A-class
the obvious creature that swims
a phrase for being away from any pool or pond

explanation.surface: A first-rate swimmer finds no pool to swim in and feels ill at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: a fish with no water really is out of its element.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person who feels awkward and out of place in unfamiliar surroundings.

clue.text: Found out how to be erudite

blocks.note: first meaning: discovered or came to know, a past-tense verb
second meaning: scholarly, deeply read, an adjective said with two syllables

explanation.surface: Someone discovered the secret of becoming highly educated.
explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling is a one-syllable verb and a two-syllable adjective, which hides the double meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned is the past tense of learn, meaning discovered, and also an adjective meaning scholarly and knowledgeable.

clue.text: Withdrew to be seen by the doctor again

blocks.note: first meaning: pulled back, as an army falling back
second meaning: split as RE- plus a word for given medical care

explanation.surface: A patient pulled out of something in order to get another appointment with the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs the word broken after RE: re-treated, given treatment a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreated means moved back or withdrew; re-treated means given medical care once more.

clue.text: Elephantine air transport

blocks.note: Jumbo was a famous elephant, and the word means huge
a jet is an aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while its two parts also build it word by word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boeing 747 and similar wide-bodied airliners are nicknamed for their enormous size, like a big elephant.

clue.text: Flag early morning departure of northern bird

indicators.note: a departure means something leaves, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: a jack is a small flag flown on a ship, as in Union Jack
dawn is the start of the day
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Someone is flagging up an early departure from the north of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small grey-naped crow, common across Europe and Britain.

clue.text: Mother once caught black snake

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an old-fashioned word for mother, hence once
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A mother of long ago managed to catch a dark-coloured snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The B goes between the third and fourth letters of the old word for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a fast, highly venomous African snake, the black mamba being the best known.

clue.text: Master in sonar made out boat propeller

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second word
made out suggests something worked out or deciphered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: MA is Master of Arts, a university degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A captain spots something on the sonar and works out what it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like a ship's captain, but it is the degree abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower drives a boat forward with oars, so is humorously a boat propeller.

clue.text: Criminal gang posed with working people in kids' sporting event

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
a machine that is working is on
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A gang of crooks poses alongside ordinary workers at a children's sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like it describes the gang, but it signals the shuffle; 'people' means a nation, not the workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional British school sports day race in which children run balancing an egg on a spoon.

clue.text: Small carriage can't possibly accommodate figure that's enormous

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so one piece is lodged inside the other
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be shuffled

blocks.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
the word without its apostrophe
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tiny carriage has no room for an enormous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't possibly' reads as a phrase, but 'can't' is the fodder and 'possibly' shuffles it with the numeral inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means of giant proportions, so huge or immense in size.

clue.text: A Glastonbury opening without mud is a fantastic sight

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
without here means outside, so the mud wraps around the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the festival's name
mire is boggy mud

explanation.surface: The opening of the Glastonbury festival without its famous mud would be too good to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury is a huge English music festival notorious for muddy fields; 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as imagined water in a desert, so an unreal sight.

clue.text: As soon as wife gets time off then?

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the named letter is removed

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A husband asks when his wife will finally get some time off.
explanation.definitionFit: When as a conjunction means at the moment that, the same as 'as soon as'.

clue.text: Sweetums is one silly tender name!

indicators.note: silly suggests nonsense, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Calling someone Sweetums is a soppy pet name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly a definition itself: the fodder 'tender name' also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetums is an example of a term of affection, a pet word lovers use for each other.

clue.text: Expert in wordplay said in French

blocks.note: a pun is a play on words
dit is French for said

explanation.surface: A specialist in puns delivers them in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A pundit is an authority who gives opinions, typically a commentator on television.

clue.text: Apprehension with soldier heading off on ship

indicators.note: a heading is the first letter, and off means it is removed

blocks.note: W is short for with
a marine is a soldier serving at sea
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A soldier sets off on a ship, full of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Wariness is caution or anxious watchfulness, a state of apprehension about danger.

clue.text: Providing relief for soldiers' condition before passing on

blocks.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
passing on is a euphemism for death

explanation.surface: Treating a soldier's illness before he dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition before' only places the soldiers ahead of the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy something is to cure or put it right, so remedying is giving relief for a problem.

clue.text: Soldiers take high ground quietly before breakfast?

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the rest

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
a ridge is a raised stretch of land

explanation.surface: Troops stealthily capture a hill before their morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: porridge is one kind of breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge, boiled oats, is a classic British morning meal, hence an example of breakfast.

clue.text: Discover some of Montreal is extraordinary

indicators.note: some of means only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: A traveller discovers that parts of the Canadian city are remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it, to find it out or discover it.

clue.text: English company has money problem without Europe's financial organisation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letter is dropped
a problem suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: E is short for English
Co is the abbreviation for company
taken as written
E is short for Europe

explanation.surface: An English firm runs into cash trouble when it is cut off from European finance.
explanation.definitionFit: An economy is the organised system of production and wealth in a country, its financial structure.

clue.text: Start anew in shift working

blocks.note: to shift something is to move it
a switched-on machine is working

explanation.surface: Someone begins again on a fresh work shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To move on is to leave the past behind and make a fresh beginning elsewhere.

clue.text: One of the undead in endless primeval dance

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter goes
a dance moves bodies around, so the letters swap places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ghoulish creature joins an ancient ritual dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire is a corpse that rises from the grave to drink blood, so neither dead nor alive.

clue.text: Work very hard on design of wood tables

indicators.note: a design is a new pattern, so the letters are laid out differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpenter toils long hours designing wooden tables.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to labour with enormous effort, figuratively straining until it hurts.

clue.text: Deer bulk up a bit to produce young

indicators.note: a bit means only a portion of the words beside it is used
in a down clue, up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Deer fatten themselves up a little before giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulk up' reads as a phrase, but 'up' turns the hidden letters round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is for animals to mate and have offspring, to bring young into the world.

clue.text: Saucy girl picked up furs

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: minks are animals prized for their fur

explanation.surface: A cheeky young woman goes shopping and buys some fur coats.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is an impudent, cunning or flirtatious girl, an old-fashioned word.

clue.text: Hit back of reckless three-wheeler

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: A careless tricycle rider crashes into something from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike is to hit or deliver a blow; as a noun it is also a blow.

clue.text: Innovative spirit in old rail organisation

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the following letters
organisation means arranging, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: O is short for old
taken as written
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A railway company of old has a new, inventive attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests mood or attitude, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Original work is new and inventive, not copied from anything earlier.

clue.text: Dine out by lake behind brother's yard when warm

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of place, so the letters are rearranged
behind puts the first group after the following piece

blocks.note: Fr is the title for a friar, a religious brother
taken as written
L is short for lake
Y is short for yard

explanation.surface: Eating out by a lake in a brother's garden when the weather is warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Brother's 's stands for 'has'; Fr also abbreviates Father, the title for a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm in manner means kindly and affectionate, as a friendly person is.

clue.text: Old man has almost nothing on — wow!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
on places one piece after the other

blocks.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
zero means nothing

explanation.surface: An elderly man is wearing next to nothing, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: A geezer is British slang for a man, often an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: Geezer is informal slang for an old fellow, a man, especially an elderly or eccentric one.
